summary_html:
The Dollar's Convenience Yield — Factor Summary

策略概述

This paper draws an analogy between CIP deviations in currency markets (the dollar's convenience yield) and deviations from forward-spot parity in commodity markets. The key equation is F_{t,T} = S_t(1 + r + u - y), where y is the convenience yield that arises when physical commodities are scarce. High convenience yield (backwardation) signals scarcity and holding value, while low/negative CY (contango) signals oversupply.

We implement this as a cross-sectional carry/convenience yield factor applied to all Chinese commodity futures. The primary signal is the roll yield (ry), which directly measures the term structure slope — a real-data proxy for convenience yield. Commodities in backwardation (high ry, high CY) are bought; commodities in contango (negative ry) are sold. The factor is enhanced by combining it with basis (spot-futures gap) as a complementary scarcity measure, since both signals reflect the same underlying economic phenomenon of commodity scarcity.

数学公式

Convenience Yield (from term structure):

y \approx \frac{S_t - F_{t,T}}{S_t} - (r + u) \quad \Rightarrow \quad \text{proxy: } ry_t

Basis Signal:

\text{basis\_ratio}_t = \frac{\text{basis}_t}{\text{close}_t}

Cross-sectional ranking (for each factor f):

\text{rank}_{i,t} = \frac{\text{Rank}(f_{i,t})}{N_t} \in [0,1]

Continuous long-short signal:

\text{signal}_{i,t} = (\text{rank}_{i,t} - 0.5) \times 2 \in [-1, 1]

Equal-weight combo (CY + Basis):

\text{combo}_{i,t} = \frac{\text{rank}^{cy}_{i,t} + \text{rank}^{basis}_{i,t}}{2}

Volatility-scaled position:

\text{position}_{i,t} = \text{signal}_{i,t} \times \frac{\sigma_{target}}{\hat{\sigma}_{i,t} \times \sqrt{252}}

改进历程

R1 (Sharpe 1.00): Initial implementation with 5 individual factors (CY level, CY EMA252, CY momentum 20d/60d, basis ratio, hedging pressure) and 3 combo variants, using 5/10/20-day rebalance. Best variant was cy_ema252_raw — smoothed convenience yield (EMA 252) as a pure carry factor. Turnover was high (0.55 daily) due to short rebalance periods. All 5 gates passed from R1.

R2 (Sharpe 1.18, +18%): Diagnosed high turnover and that cross-sectional signal was effective (IC=0.017) while time-series IC was near zero. Actions: (1) Increased default rebalance to 20 days to reduce turnover; (2) Added sym_rolling_ic_gate to filter weak symbols; (3) Added EMA-smoothed basis variant; (4) Enabled _cs/_ts normalization. The CY+Basis equal-weight combo emerged as the best (1.18), outperforming standalone CY (1.00). Turnover dropped from 0.55 to 0.31.

R3 (Sharpe 1.22, +3.4%): Explored weighted combos and vol window sensitivity. Key finding: longer vol window (120 days vs 60) improved the CY+Basis combo by better estimating slower-moving commodity volatility regimes. Weighted combos did not improve significantly over equal-weight. Three-factor combo (adding hedge pressure) slightly underperformed the two-factor version. Final turnover: 0.29.

Key turning point: R2's combination of CY + Basis was the biggest improvement (+18%). The paper's theoretical insight that both convenience yield and basis reflect scarcity validated empirically — the two signals are complementary despite measuring related phenomena.

适用说明

  • Data frequency: Daily
  • Universe: All commodity futures (~49 liquid symbols with CY/basis data)
  • Holding period: ~20 trading days
  • Factor type: Cross-sectional carry/scarcity (primarily)
  • Known limitations:
- Relies on ry and basis fields (37% and 28% non-null respectively); symbols without term structure data are excluded

- Time-series IC is low (~0.007) — this is fundamentally a cross-sectional factor, not a timing signal - Moderately correlated (0.79) with existing CY/basis factors in the library, but delivers higher Sharpe - Yearly Sharpe varies: strongest in 2018-2022, weaker in 2016-2017 and 2023-2025
